meta.what: National Priorities List sites per county and year (2015-2025): active (listed by Dec 31 and not deleted by then), listed in the year, deleted in the year, construction complete by Dec 31 (cumulative).

source.name: EPA Superfund National Priorities List (NPL) Sites with Status Information

counties.source: TIGERweb https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Generalized_ACS2023/State_County/MapServer layer 13 (Counties 20M: the 50 states, DC and Puerto Rico; Connecticut as planning regions); adjacency from https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/reference/county_adjacency/county_adjacency2023.txt.

meta.join: (State, County) to FIPS by normalised name; fails closed (unmatched and ambiguous names are listed, never guessed). Connecticut's NPL rows name legacy counties and do not match ACS2023 planning regions.
meta.zeroRule: A county in counties.json that is not in `places` and not in `nullPlaces` has 0 for every feature and year: the NPL list is complete for the United States.
meta.nullRule: A county a site could be in but was not placed in is null for every feature and year, listed in `nullPlaces` with the reason: join:multi_county (EPA lists the site in several counties, all named), join:ambiguous_county_or_city (a bare name where the state has both the county and the independent city), or join:unmatched_site_in_state (the name, or any one name in a multi-county list, matched nothing, so the site could be in any county of its state and every county of that state is null, e.g. Connecticut's legacy counties and Alaska's Outer Ketchikan). A county string is matched whole first, so a single county named with 'and' (Lewis and Clark, MT; King and Queen, VA) is one county; lists are split only on commas and slashes.
